key_insight: GroundCount reduces counting hallucinations in vision–language models by explicitly grounding them with object detections (bounding boxes + instance counts), combining the localization strengths of detectors with the reasoning strengths of VLMs.
problem_solved: VLMs frequently hallucinate numeric answers in counting tasks (low counting accuracy despite strong visual reasoning elsewhere); GroundCount addresses unreliable counting by injecting explicit, detector-derived spatial and instance information into the VLM pipeline.
method: Run a lightweight object detector (e.g., YOLO) to produce bounding boxes, class labels, and instance counts for an input image.
Integrate detector outputs into the VLM via grounding tokens/adapter layers or prompt augmentation so the model conditions on explicit spatial instances when answering count queries.
Aggregate detector-backed evidence (e.g., filter/merge detections, consensus counting) while preserving the VLM for higher-level reasoning — minimal compute overhead, improved numerical fidelity.
impact: Provides a practical, low-overhead way to make VLM outputs more reliable for counting and instance-level queries, enabling safer and more accurate use in VQA, inventory, robotics, and scene understanding workloads.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image → object detector (boxes) → GroundCount fusion → VLM answer (highlight grounding flow)
Side-by-side bar chart: counting accuracy with baseline VLM vs. GroundCount across several benchmarks
Annotated example image: detections overlaid with counts and the final model answer (shows corrected vs. hallucinated count)
Compute vs. accuracy scatter: demonstrates minimal latency/compute increase for large gain in counting accuracy
paper_title: GroundCount: Grounding Vision-Language Models with Object Detection for Mitigating Counting Hallucinations
paper_authors: Boyuan Chen, Minghao Shao, Siddharth Garg, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique
